Description: Nature of Complaint: Gross Negligence, Extreme Departure from the Standard of Care, Unprofessional Conduct (Solicitation of Illegal Acts), and Failure to Establish/Provide Care under Dangerous Circumstances.

Detailed Description:
I attended a scheduled intake evaluation with Dr. Paula Bailey-Walton, a board-certified Addiction Medicine specialist. I was specifically referred to this evaluation by a New Directions counselor who assured me Dr. Bailey-Walton was equipped to medically manage a taper off of Xanax (a short-acting benzodiazepine).

During the clinical intake, rather than establishing a safe treatment plan, Dr. Bailey-Walton exhibited a severe and dangerous departure from the standard of care:

Solicitation of Illegal Black-Market Activity: Instead of initiating a standard medical taper (such as a transition to a longer-acting benzodiazepine), Dr. Bailey-Walton explicitly asked if I could "find any longer-acting benzos off of the street" where I was getting the Xanax. When I stated no, she provided no medical oversight, effectively instructing a prospective patient to use the illicit drug market to self-manage a highly dangerous withdrawal syndrome.

Inappropriate Prescribing Practices: When asked how she treats dependency, she stated she only uses Naltrexone for alcohol and Suboxone for opioids. Despite knowing I was already established on Suboxone, and despite Suboxone having absolutely no pharmacological efficacy for benzodiazepine withdrawal, she ended the encounter by asking if I was "ok on the Suboxone" and "did I need any help with that," attempting to push an unsolicited controlled substance rather than treating the acute condition I presented for.

Inappropriate Delegation / Refusal to Treat: Despite operating as a specialist and conducting a formal intake for a patient actively seeking help, Dr. Bailey-Walton refused to provide direct medical management. Even after I informed her that I had already attempted to utilize county resources, she initiated a call to the Los Angeles County substance abuse helpline (SASH) during our session. Turfing an acute, high-risk patient sitting in her office to a generalized county triage line—after her own facility's staff assured me she would provide medical management—constitutes an egregious failure to treat.

Dr. Bailey-Walton's instruction to procure controlled substances from street dealers is a gross ethical violation. Her actions put my immediate physical safety at extreme risk. I request the Board investigate her intake protocols, her prescribing practices, and her solicitation of illegal patient activity.
